surprises.head: Vancouver brought the hits
surprises.body: Vancouver is one of the league’s lightest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 161 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 82 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: The Canucks shake off a slow start
paras: Luke Schenn and Adam Klapka dropped the gloves early in the first. Matt Coronato opened the scoring for the Flames on the power play late in the period, but they didn’t score again. It was a busy third period. Liam Öhgren tied it 1-1 for Vancouver early in the period, and Elias Pettersson (#25) put the Canucks up 2-1 midway through the period. Drew O'Connor made it 3-1 with three and a half minutes left, and that was that. Aatu Räty added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 4-1.

The Canucks carried the play, and got the result to match. The Canucks had five shots in the first period and trailed 1-0, then outshot the Flames 21-13 the rest of the way. Leevi Meriläinen made 23 saves for the Canucks, and Devin Cooley stopped 22 of 25. By our Swing measure, Linus Karlsson had the best night of anyone. The Canucks moved to 2-1-0, and the Flames dropped to 0-2-0.

items.text: Elias Pettersson (#40) passed Alexander Edler for eighth on the Canucks’ all-time assists list, with 311.
